### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5908a8d98606c27eed036c193534de1744ccfc68` — the merge of head `f1bd927df4cf1c8e86d14daba55a856d8e44677d` into base `49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5908a8d98606c27eed036c193534de1744ccfc68 && git checkout 5908a8d98606c27eed036c193534de1744ccfc68
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 f1bd927df4cf1c8e86d14daba55a856d8e44677d && git checkout -B drift-repro 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2 && git merge --no-ff f1bd927df4cf1c8e86d14daba55a856d8e44677d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

- **形态**: `l1-face.mjs --pr 37073`: 12 ok, 1 flag (changeset, judged below). Open, draft, base `main`; first line `Part of #36646`, no closing keyword anywhere near another card. `Part of` is right: the card asks for the queue p90 back under budget, and the PR itself says it alone is not shown to do that. #36646 keeps `pm:dispatched` (landing rule B); this PR's merge closes nothing.
- **前提实测**: own run at the head, in `packages/cli`. `vitest run --project unit test/vitest-slices.test.ts` gave 17/17 pass. End to end through vitest's own sharding, `OS_TEST_SHARD=k/3` with a test-name filter matching nothing: slices of 141 / 151 / 152 files, 0 duplicates, union 444 distinct, all 5 `DECLARATION_READER_FILES` in slice 1. That is the dev's reading, reproduced. The "every file runs exactly once" pin holds. `planSlices` assigns each entry exactly once by construction (readers in one pass, the rest in one pass), and the sequencer keeps `slices[i] === index`. The battery pins disjoint plus union at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 slices, order independence, and the live population at 3 slices. Determinism across slice processes: the weight sort breaks ties by path and the input order is irrelevant (pinned).
- **门禁 check-runs**: at `96c83ea0`: 37 success, 21 expected skip, 0 unexpected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates success, TypeScript Type Check success. The dev's local ledger is split across `9b0861a2` (53/53, `--ran` 0 unrun) and the head (the seven families the last test-only commit touches, re-run). The CI check-runs on the head are the reading of record.
- **接受的偏差**: the fix lands at the producer `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` plus a new `packages/cli/vitest-slices.ts`, not at the claim's declared `scripts/ci/**`. This is the dispatch-runbook producer clause ("若实测表明真正的生产者在别包,直接按生产者侧修,落点与理由写进报告和 PR 正文"), and both the report and the PR body give the place and the reason. Note for the seat: `packages/cli` is outside area f2-E's lease paths, and the claim's file surface was not amended. `overlap-check` was clean before each push. The seat confirms no other lane holds `packages/cli` in flight before landing. Also accepted: the removed reader-fit throw (readers are now seeded, so there is no count bound left to break).
- **数字标注**: the before figures are queue readings (620 green merge_group runs, run ids named). Every after figure is labelled as a planner replay ("a prediction from measured per-file readings, not a queue reading"; "Queue reading after: NOT MEASURED"; the #36637 figure "Planner prediction, not a reading"). The module header says "Replayed on those five runs' readings". Nothing is presented as a measured queue improvement.
- **范围外去向**: `Skills-docs:` not owed (kind `none`). The report's out-of-scope item is the shard-timings weekly refresh going unlanded for three weeks, carrier: seat (refresh lane). There are two `open_questions` for the seat: (1) land the green generated refresh #36637, the larger lever per the dev's planner replay; (2) further tail levers. Of these, (A) a parallel CLI slice leg is `ci.yml`, Tier H, and (B) a fourth slice is refused by the partitioner's slice-count ruling. The dev recommends re-reading the queue after #36637 and this PR land.
- **changeset**: `skip-changeset` is right. `@objectstack/cli` ships `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and its build `rootDir` is `src`. The new module and the config sit at the package root, outside `src`, so nothing in this diff ships. The dev's positive-control read agrees: `dist` has zero `planSlices` hits, and `SCAFFOLD_PNPM_RANGE` hits `dist/commands/create.d.ts`. The label went on with the relay `pr_create`; there was no refused command.
- **落地条款**: `check-governed-merges --pr 37073`: NOT governed, 376 lines. This is an ordinary area landing. `landing-k --pr 37073`: K = 44 ≥ 15, so **merge main first** (no rebase). The merge moves the head, so the checks must go green again on the new head before arming. The L1 verdict carries over a clean merge of main that does not touch these four files; re-send it here if the merge has conflicts in them.
